summary: Former state fire lookout on Shaffer Mountain, Lassen County, set up in 1931 and replaced in 1949 by a lookout near Eagle Lake; summit now has towers.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts page marks the lookout removed; the summit now carries wind-measuring and communication towers.

access.note: BLM land. A public road reaches close to the summit; a gate about a quarter mile from the top restricts access. Source is a climbing guide, not checked on the ground.

visit.trail_note: Road starts at US 395, about 6 miles north of Litchfield; the gate sits about a quarter mile below the summit.

events.note: State fire lookout set up on the summit; a May 1931 newspaper item reports a ranger surveying the station site.
Several acres of brush and grazing land burned on ranches near the James Mapes property; the attendant at the Schaffer Peak lookout located it.
A June 1946 item says a lookout had been stationed on the mountain.
Two Lassen County blog posts say the lookout ran until 1949; SummitPost gives 1947.
Replaced with Landon Lookout near Eagle Lake.

notes_for_editor: Not checked on the ground. Spelling varies: Shaffer, Schaffer (the 1940 item says Schaffer Peak). Elevation differs: Peakbagging lists 6739 ft, a blog post says 6375 ft; elevation is not used. The FFLA list gives no NHLR or FFLOS number for this site, and the NHLR and FFLOS pages could not be reached, so no registration is claimed. Landon Lookout near Eagle Lake may be the Greens Peak lookout (us-ca-don-landon-greens-peak); not confirmed.
